title: Hosea
lead: Hosea son of Beeri was a prophet of the northern kingdom in the last decades before the Assyrian conquest in 722 BC, and the only writing prophet from the north. His book opens the Twelve. It has 14 chapters (197 verses): his marriage and the names of three children (1-3), the LORD's case against Israel, its priests and its kings (4-11), and a closing group of Jacob, death and the call to return (12-14).

sections.b: The heading dates Hosea by Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah and Jeroboam son of Joash of Israel. Jeroboam II's long reign (2 Kings 14:23-29) was the north's last time of wealth. After his death Israel had six kings in about thirty years, four of them killed by their successors (2 Kings 15), and Assyria under Tiglath-pileser III took Galilee (733-732 BC) and, under Shalmaneser V and Sargon II, Samaria (722 BC; the date 721 has been argued). Hosea's oracles run from the late years of Jeroboam to the eve of the fall.

Hosea 1:10 and 2:23 are quoted in Romans 9:25-26 and echoed in 1 Peter 2:10; Hosea 6:6 in Matthew 9:13 and 12:7; Hosea 10:8 in Luke 23:30 and Revelation 6:16; Hosea 11:1 in Matthew 2:15; Hosea 13:14 in 1 Corinthians 15:55; and Hosea 14:2 in Hebrews 13:15 (in the Greek form).
